entries.basis: The engraved Violin I part (source42-103548.pdf pp.1-3) is in treble clef and sits high above the staff for long stretches, with a rest-filled 3/8 scherzo: bars of slurred repeated 16ths in the opening (p.1), long sustained high notes with a dotted tremolo-like marking (p.2, ledger lines above the staff), and about 40 bars of one slurred 16th-note cell repeated on the top of the E string, ending on sustained very high notes (p.3). The ff and fff dynamics and high-position security are real, but the figure is mechanical and repeated, not varied virtuoso passagework, so the 'extreme' wording of the level-8 opinion is overstated and the repeated-cell endurance does not reach the Bacewicz anchor at 7. The handwritten score (source42-103546.pdf pp.1-2) shows the lower parts on ostinato repeated 16ths and displaced entries on rests, with no clear ensemble demand beyond the notes, so no uplift. Six is the best fit; the level-6 opinion's reading of the notation held up, the level-8 and level-7 readings overrated the repetition.

Coordinator score check overrode the adjudicator level of 4: PDF pp.4–5 bars 37–47 give cello 1 sustained slurred chromatic semiquavers in tenor clef with register changes, which the adjudicator said were absent, then detached Allegro moderato figures. This is advanced writing without diploma-level density, so 5, the middle opinion.

Coordinator score check overrode the adjudicator level of 4: the first-cello part (PDF p.7) has slurred chromatic demisemiquaver runs in the Adagio, sustained high tenor-clef cantabile, harmonics and treble-clef writing up high. Mostly slow with no fast passagework, so not 6; above 3. Five is the middle opinion.

Coordinator score check (44997.pdf p.6 and the graders' cited pages): Allegro with chromatic semiquaver chains in all three voices, trills and high-register violin 1. Demanding and exposed but tonal and idiomatic, without diploma-level virtuoso density throughout, so 6.

Coordinator score check (606686.pdf p.2): continuous atonal chromatic semiquavers with wide leaps at quarter=100, in tight canon across four violins, then 6/8 bariolage at dotted quarter=150 in the finale. The pitch material and ensemble precision outweigh the low positions, so 7.

Coordinator score check (1009520.pdf p.41 and the graders' cited pages): cello 1 stays largely in tenor clef with upper-position cantabile, triplets and dotted figures, but rhythms are simple and there is no sustained fast passagework, so early advanced.
